experiments.title: Nicole’s 8B Fed text arm awaits Llama-3.1-8B weights
experiments.question: Does Llama-3.1-8B(frozen)+CNN(frozen)~Pool~Add improve 20/30-minute forecasts over the frozen price baseline on FED-PXTX-ALL-REL5-v2 validation?
experiments.configuration: Frozen full-float32 Llama-3.1-8B; masked mean, first 2048 tokens; frozen CNN seeds 0/1/2 trained on FED-PX-REL5-v1; text head trains on 171 FED-PXTX-ALL-REL5-v2 rows after 2 exclusions; scores 149 validation rows. Fixed 30-epoch pilot, train-only text scaling, real/zero/past-only shuffled text.
experiments.finding: Exact one-H200 training job submitted on explicit user hold, pinned to merged main 013ca5c. Training has not started and no GPU time is consumed. On November 25 Adaeze staged the frozen CNN bundle on Drive (01 Results and Evidence/fed-spx-endpoints-price-v1-frozen-cnn.zip); its three checkpoint SHA-256s match the published metrics.json. Release still awaits the exact Llama-3.1-8B weights, which are not on Adaeze's laptop or shared Delta.
experiments.limitations: No end-to-end 8B smoke or accuracy result. Validation is exploratory; ALL contains inferred evidence classes. Exact Llama-3.1-8B weights remain missing; val-paired.npz in the CNN bundle has no published hash. Final test remains reserved and final evidence level remains undecided.

experiments.title: Price-only baselines on FED-PXTX-ALL-REL5-v2 validation
experiments.question: After correcting the release-text checks (v2), how do Persistence, the frozen none+CNN~none~none, none+DLinear~none~none and none+Ridge~none~none compare on the text-verified validation releases?
experiments.configuration: Same frozen forecasters as fed-spx-matched-control-v1, all trained on FED-PX-REL5-v1 train (978 releases). Scored on FED-PXTX-ALL-REL5-v2 validation: 149 releases, 139 release instants, 125 dates, unit weight per instant, paired 10-date block intervals. Test not loaded.
experiments.finding: Persistence MAE 16.155 / 20.484 bp at 20 / 30 minutes. none+CNN~none~none 16.057 / 20.392 bp (gain +0.088 / +0.054 bp, intervals include zero). none+DLinear~none~none 16.751 / 20.892 bp and none+Ridge~none~none 19.295 / 23.928 bp are worse than Persistence.
experiments.limitations: Validation only; CNN epochs were selected on the 207 FED-PX-REL5-v1 validation rows, which contain these 149. Inferred evidence classes are included. Intervals of about +/-0.3 bp mean only a text gain of roughly half a basis point or more can register.

figure.alt: Grouped bars of validation MAE at 20 and 30 minutes on 149 releases. Persistence and the frozen CNN are nearly equal; DLinear is about 0.6 bp higher and ridge about 3 bp higher.

experiments.title: Frozen price-only control on the text-matched Fed/SPX validation set
experiments.question: On the Fed releases whose exact text is verified, how do the frozen price-only CNN control, persistence, DLinear and ridge compare for 20- and 30-minute SPX Close forecasts?
experiments.configuration: Frozen three-seed compact CNN from fed-spx-endpoints-price-v1 (trained on 978 price-eligible train releases; exact CUDA replay). DLinear and ridge refitted on the same 978 releases and target. Scored on the 123 text-verified validation releases (113 release instants, 105 dates) with unit weight per release instant and paired 10-date block intervals. Test not loaded.
experiments.finding: Persistence MAE was 17.707 / 22.058 bp at 20 / 30 minutes. The CNN control was 17.615 / 22.042 bp, a gain of +0.082 / -0.002 bp with intervals including zero. DLinear (18.340 / 22.736 bp) and ridge (21.027 / 26.263 bp) were worse than persistence.
experiments.limitations: Validation only. CNN checkpoint epochs were chosen on the 207 price-eligible validation rows, which contain these 123, so its validation score is optimistic. Intervals of about +/-0.3 bp mean only a text gain of roughly half a basis point or more can register. The cohort includes inferred evidence classes; the strictest-evidence subset has 27 rows. The bar clock is empirically supported.

figure.alt: Grouped bars of validation MAE at 20 and 30 minutes on 123 text-matched releases. Persistence and the price CNN control are nearly equal; DLinear is slightly higher and ridge about 3 to 4 bp higher.

experiments.title: Compact price-only Fed/SPX endpoint control
experiments.question: Does the compact CNN improve on zero return for 20- and 30-minute SPX Close forecasts given only pre-release prices?
experiments.configuration: Frozen Fed/SPX alignment v1; 35 pre-release OHLC inputs and 20- and 30-minute Close returns from the forecast origin. RTX 4060, seeds 0–2, 30 epochs, 20-minute validation MAE checkpoint selection. 978 train and 207 shared validation events, with unit weight per release instant.
experiments.finding: Mean CNN MAE was 15.318 bp versus 15.343 bp for zero return at 20 minutes and 19.706 versus 19.701 bp at 30 minutes. Both paired block-bootstrap intervals for improvement include zero.
experiments.limitations: Validation only, checkpoint selection uses 20-minute validation MAE, and the bar clock is empirically supported. All 1,185 price-eligible rows have news evidence dispositions. The combined manifest has 150 train and 88 validation rows under all audit rules, or 90 train and 25 validation rows excluding the inferred minutes and speech classes. The matched news model and held-out evaluation remain pending.

figure.alt: Zero-return and compact price-only MAE are nearly identical at 20 and 30 minutes, and both paired intervals include zero.

evidence.label: Independent FOMC minutes and Fed speech audit
Combined Fed/SPX news cohort and audit comparison

experiments.title: Fed/SPX price-only validation baselines
experiments.question: How accurately can pre-announcement SPX price history forecast the OHLC path around official Fed releases, and does ridge improve on last-close persistence?
experiments.configuration: Joye's Fed/SPX alignment v1, frozen CAMEF SP500.csv, 35 pre-release bars and 140 target bars. Ridge alpha 10 on 1,013 main train events. Paired validation on 215 main and 85 flagged events with unit weighting per announcement instant within each cohort.
experiments.finding: Last-close persistence had lower main validation OHLC path MAE at 35, 70 and 140 bars. At 140 bars the MAEs were 75.10 bp for persistence and 78.26 bp for ridge. Ridge improvement was −4.21% with a paired 95% interval of [−8.77%, −0.48%] using ten announcement dates per block.
experiments.limitations: Validation only, fixed ridge penalty, and one historical validation period. Flagged intervals span zero. Forecast paths overlap and H140 crosses overnight. DLinear and a price-only counterpart to the text model await evaluation on this split. The held-out test awaits the frozen matched comparison.

figure.alt: On 215 main validation rows, last-close persistence has lower OHLC path MAE than ridge at each of 35, 70 and 140 bars. All three paired 95% improvement intervals favor persistence.

experiments.configuration: Separate Fed/daily Treasury pilot; 36/12 train/validation statements, 180/60 windows, matched seeds 23–25 and 10 fixed epochs. Four paired cells, shared frozen yield branch, gate fit on chronological train-only OOF predictions.

figure.alt: Validation MAE: no change 9.950 bp, frozen yields 11.830, pooled 11.787 ungated and 11.810 gated, cross-attention 12.200 ungated and 11.976 gated.

experiments.finding: No change led at 9.950 bp MAE. Cross-attention was 0.413 bp worse than pooled without a gate, and 0.166 bp worse with one. The gate softened the cross-attention penalty but did not rescue it. Prior-statement text matched or slightly beat the current statement in all four cells.
experiments.limitations: Repeated validation only: 12 statements and overlapping origins; no held-out test, no C1/equity result, no verified historical minute-level availability. Paired bootstrap is descriptive.
experiments.question: Does querying individual statement tokens from frozen yield history improve over pooled text, with and without a learned gate?
experiments.title: Compact Treasury: cross-attention and gate ablation
Compact price-only: endpoint direction-loss ablation
experiments.question: Does an endpoint close-return sign penalty improve direction without worse whole-path MAE?
experiments.configuration: Canonical screened C1; 6,167 train / 2,302 validation; L35/H140 and matched seeds 0, 1, 2 on RTX 4060. Same Smooth L1 loss with or without a weight-1 sign penalty at close H35/H70/H140. Validation whole-path MAE selects both arms.
experiments.finding: Penalty raised path MAE from 82.626 to 82.674 bp and lowered H140 direction hit rate by 1.173 percentage points. Both effects had the same sign in every seed; H35/H70 direction barely changed. Keep Smooth L1 as the default.
experiments.limitations: Validation only, no text or test scoring; one loss form, weight, set of horizons and checkpoint selector; no paired uncertainty interval.

figure.alt: With the sign penalty, mean validation direction accuracy moved −0.043, +0.043 and −1.173 percentage points at H35, H70 and H140.

experiments.title: Compact whole-path baseline and summary residual
experiments.question: Does an independently trained summary encoder improve the same lightweight price model on R3's full OHLC return target?
experiments.configuration: RTX 4060; canonical screened C1; 35 observed and 140 future OHLC bars; seeds 0–2. The price + summary residual holds its same-seed price model fixed. All six checkpoints were selected by validation whole-path MAE and evaluated with a locked test configuration.
experiments.finding: Price + summary improved validation (82.403 vs. 82.626 bp) but not locked test (80.341 vs. 80.295 bp price-only, 80.487 zero; 2,236 events). Keep compact price-only as the forward baseline and evaluate further variants on validation.
experiments.limitations: Archive summaries, not original articles; forecast-time availability and near duplicates remain unverified. Test effects were mixed across seeds and no uncertainty interval was estimated. R3's published result is context only; per-event pairing and superiority over R3 were not independently established.

figure.alt: Across three validation seeds, adding event summaries lowered average full-path MAE from 82.626 to 82.403 basis points. The zero-return baseline was 83.636.

evidence.label: Locked test scores, provenance, and limits

experiments.title: Compact laptop price and pooled-text residual model
experiments.question: Can pooled article features add useful error reduction to an independently fitted compact price forecast within laptop resource targets?
experiments.configuration: compact_features.py exports a checksum/signature-verified existing pooled cache without LLM loading; train_compact.py fits price first, freezes it, then fits the tiny text correction. 82598 total parameters for 2048-dimensional text; training-only feature normalization; H35/70/140 endpoints; three past-date donor controls and paired date-block intervals. Portable NPZ with --include-prices plus receipt allows local training without raw articles/backbones; default run_local.ps1 mode is multimodal.
experiments.finding: Feature integrity/mapping, donor chronology, frozen-price residual fitting and aligned text-control tests passed on synthetic fixtures. Full real-data training/evaluation pending.
experiments.limitations: Actual RTX4060 CUDA synthetic execution passed, but no real-market accuracy, T4 execution or raw-article encoding latency is verified. Current shared CUDA packages are reused through a working project-local interpreter; no shared environment was overwritten. Timestamp availability remains unverified.

evidence.label: Synthetic RTX4060 execution timing, not quality

experiments.finding: No new full execution or measured quality finding. Updated audit-first design and testable controls; intended executor Nicole Lyu.
experiments.limitations: Intraday publication times remain unverified. CPU code checks do not certify full-backbone GPU execution or performance. No benefit is assumed; new attempts require exact compute/input provenance.

experiments.title: Did a simple model gain from the correct article?
experiments.question: Do frozen article embeddings improve 35-bar close-return forecasts over prices and event metadata?
experiments.configuration: Frozen screened C1. Price and metadata ridge models with matched and reassigned pooled Llama embeddings. All comparisons use the same held-out rows.
experiments.finding: The matched-article model reached 64.721 bp MAE versus 64.462 bp with prices and metadata alone. Reassigning articles at test time changed MAE by 0.020 bp.
experiments.limitations: Results cover 2,191 eligible held-out events and one pooled representation at the 35-bar endpoint. Retained article release times are unverified.

figure.alt: Relative MAE intervals for matched article forecasts versus price and metadata, a reassigned training control, and a test-time reassignment control.

experiments.title: Does the Q-Former update after the Stage 3 fix?
experiments.question: Do the Q-Former projection and LayerNorm weights change during Stage 3 after PR #28?
experiments.configuration: R3 return flags with Q-Former and a softmax gate on frozen screened C1. Seed 0, one epoch per stage, batch 2, 16 training events and 8 per evaluation split. One H200 on Nicole’s personal GPU resource.
experiments.finding: The smoke passed. The projection norm moved from zero to 0.02359 and the LayerNorm weights changed during Stage 3.
experiments.limitations: Small execution smoke on a single seed. Forecasting performance requires a matched full evaluation.

figure.alt: Projection norm increased from zero to 0.02359. LayerNorm weights changed by up to 0.0000401.

experiments.title: R3 got almost the same result with shuffled news
experiments.question: Does the R3 return model forecast better with the correctly matched article?
experiments.configuration: Nicole ran Adaeze’s exact seed-0 R3 setup on one H200. Both article checks used the same model, 2,236 screened events across 845 dates, and three shuffle draws.
experiments.finding: Average return error was 80.615 basis points with the correct article, 80.618 with shuffled articles, and 80.487 for a simple zero-return forecast.
experiments.limitations: The paired 95% interval for the small matched-article gain includes zero. This is one seed. The earlier R2 used different hardware, and retained article release times remain unverified.

figure.alt: Correct and shuffled articles gave almost identical R3 return error. The paired 95% interval includes zero.

experiments.title: The last-price rule beat both trained approaches
experiments.question: Does adding articles during training improve price forecasts beyond a trained price-only model and a simple last-price forecast?
experiments.configuration: Two price-only models started from matching price-pretraining checkpoints and trained for two more epochs. Each single-H200 job took about three minutes including checks and evaluation. Both scored the same 2,236 screened test events across 845 dates.
experiments.finding: At 140 bars, news-trained models had 12.5% and 26.2% lower error than the matched price-only models. Repeating the last prices also had 8.2% and 18.2% lower error than those news-trained models.
experiments.limitations: The training packages differ in their warm-up, fusion and auxiliary objectives. The earlier article swaps showed little advantage for a particular article. Retained publication times remain unverified.

figure.alt: The last-price forecast had the lowest 140-bar error for both seeds. News-trained models beat their trained price-only references.

evidence.label: Why the test set has 2,236 examples

experiments.title: Repeating the last prices beat the first news model
experiments.question: Could a flat forecast beat the first news model on the exact same test examples?
experiments.configuration: Reused the saved seed-0 predictions on 2,236 events and 845 dates. Repeated the last value of each price channel. Paired uncertainty groups nearby event dates.
experiments.finding: The last-price rule had 20.81%, 15.85% and 8.21% lower error at 35, 70 and 140 bars. All paired intervals favored the simple rule. Swapping articles changed predictions by less than 0.5% of the model’s typical forecast error.
experiments.limitations: This comparison used seed 0. It establishes the result for a simple flat forecast on these examples. The repeat’s full predictions were outside this analysis, and retained article release times remain unverified.

figure.alt: Repeating the last prices reduced error at all three horizons in seed 0. The whiskers show paired 95% date-block intervals.

experiments.title: A second run found no clear article advantage
experiments.question: Does the near-zero correct-versus-shuffled text gap persist with a second training seed?
experiments.configuration: Training seed 1 on the frozen screened dataset. batch 8; two epochs per stage; stride 10; TF32; no 4-bit; cross-attention; softmax gate; raw TS residual; no learnable last value. Evaluated on the same 2,236 test events with three shuffle draws.
experiments.finding: The correct article showed no clear forecasting advantage at any of the three forecast lengths. At 140 bars, the correct article’s estimated improvement in mean squared error was +0.0085% (95% interval -0.0061% to +0.0244%).
experiments.limitations: Each interval describes one trained model and three shuffle draws. Training effects can vary across seeds. The release times of retained articles remain unverified. The shuffled article is a diagnostic comparison and can come from later test dates. The article-free controls remove text during prediction. Training a price-only model is a separate comparison.

figure.alt: Paired text-control improvements with date-block intervals across three forecast horizons

experiments.title: Correct articles barely changed price error
experiments.question: Does the model forecast prices better with the correct article than with a randomly reassigned article?
experiments.configuration: Frozen screened C1 price task, 2,236 test events. MOMENT and Llama backbones, cross-attention, softmax gate, 2 epochs per stage, batch 8, one H200. Three shuffled-article draws and two article-free controls. Training seed 0.
experiments.finding: Correct and shuffled articles produced nearly identical errors at 35, 70 and 140 bars. The uncertainty intervals all include zero.
experiments.limitations: One checkpoint and three shuffle draws. Retained release times remain unverified. Removing text at prediction time differs from training a price-only model.

figure.alt: The real-versus-shuffled text error estimates sit near zero at all three forecast horizons.

experiments.title: Volatility did not reveal a clear text benefit
experiments.question: Did the average hide a benefit from the right article when prices had been moving more sharply?
experiments.configuration: Reused the seed-0 predictions. Grouped events by volatility before the forecast using training-data thresholds. Tested four date-block lengths.
experiments.finding: The real-versus-shuffled gap remained near zero in every group. The high-volatility group had 1,018 events across 382 dates.
experiments.limitations: Same checkpoint as the first price experiment. This exploratory analysis measured price movement before the forecast. It did not identify unexpected news shocks or test differences between groups.

figure.alt: The left panel shows no clear difference between matched and shuffled articles in low, medium or high prior volatility.

experiments.title: Which changes help return forecasts?
experiments.question: Which of the three return-model changes improves forecasting under the same conditions?
experiments.configuration: Frozen screened C1. R0→R1 adds a direction term, R1→R2 updates gate supervision, and R2→R3 enables a learnable last-value shortcut.
experiments.finding: R0–R2 finished on Delta. At the latest Delta check, its R3 and paired article runs were queued. A separate H200 R3 replay completed and is linked below.
experiments.limitations: These are descriptive differences from one seed. The paired article checks are needed before drawing a conclusion about matched text on the return task.

evidence.label: Completed R3 replay on one H200

experiments.title: Fixing padding changed attention more than forecasts
experiments.question: Did correcting the Q-Former padding mask improve forecasting?
experiments.configuration: Original positional split. Matched one before/after Q-Former run. 16 queries, two layers, batch 8, two epochs per stage.
experiments.finding: Attention on padding fell from 34% to 0%. Test MSE changed from 6.33 to 6.32 × 10⁻⁴.
experiments.limitations: Single unseeded run and historical split with known window overlap. The before run used a different machine. Keep this diagnosis separate from screened C1 results.

figure.alt: Attention on padding fell from 34 percent to zero, while test error barely changed.

experiments.title: Does expert routing help on screened data?
experiments.question: Do routed experts improve return forecasts compared with a matching reference?
experiments.configuration: Requires a matching R3 return reference, same frozen data, training budget, seed, and hardware environment.
experiments.finding: In Joye’s historical run, routing varied by event category, while the experts gave text similar weights. A verified screened comparison is still pending.
experiments.limitations: Keep the historical diagnostics separate and use the owner’s configuration before scheduling any new work.
